script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The cheering section adds a group the passage does not mention.
The line about nobody being able to look two directions at once suggests they could not both rely on Egypt and seek the LORD. The passage says they did not seek Him, not that they could not.
The imagined line “let me rephrase that” puts made-up words in God’s mouth.
The passage does not say the words were spoken out loud.
The lion is not terrified or subdued, but the passage does not say it does not move an inch.
The fruit basket breaks the food rule for jokes and comparisons.
The passage says their hands made the idols, but does not say they bowed to them.
Papa Dorin is a cookie stamper; saying he makes cookies with his stamper suggests he uses a separate one.
The passage says they will reject the idols on that day, not that their hands turn from them now.
The passage does not say that no army carries the sword.
The passage does not say the trouble started in Egypt or that the sword was not forged by anyone. It says it was not made by mortals.
The passage does not say that no human army holds the sword.
Saying he would be running with Assyria puts Papa Dorin inside a Bible event.
The passage does not say there is no swinging or shouting, or that a banner shows up by itself.
